title_prefix: txospenderindex has no startup rewind, s
mechanism: The mechanism the finding names is real and I reproduced it, but the harm runs the OTHER way. txospender-index defines no INDEX-PREPARE-SYNC method, so it inherits the base no-op (src/storage/index-base.lisp:115-121); only blockfilterindex and coinstatsindex have one (src/node/indexes.lisp:22, :47). Its INDEX-HEIGHT method declares (ignore chainstate) and returns the raw stored height (src/storage/txospenderindex.lisp:55-57). CATCH-UP-INDEX therefore calls a no-op prepare and then guards the backfill with (when (< (index-height index cs) tip) ...) (src/node/indexes.lisp:99-114): a marker naming a block on an ABANDONED branch at a height at or above the active tip passes neither test, so nothing is rewound AND nothing is backfilled. Core does both in one place: BaseIndex::Sync detects that the stored best block is not the parent of the next block to index and calls Rewind (refs/bitcoin/src/index/base.cpp:239), which walks pprev calling CustomRemove per block (:290, :313); TxoSpenderIndex opts into disconnect_data (refs/bitcoin/src/index/txospenderindex.cpp:76) and implements CustomRemove (:136), so the abandoned branch's rows are erased and the fork-point-to-tip range is then indexed forward. Our INDEX-REWIND-BLOCK for this index exists but is reachable only from the live :block-disconnected hook (src/node/indexes.lisp:252), which cannot fire for blocks disconnected while the process was down. The index also has no contiguity refusal: its INDEX-WRITE-BLOCK returns (values t nil) unconditionally (src/storage/txospenderindex.lisp:62-67), so unlike blockfilterindex (the only :noncontiguous producer in the tree, src/storage/blockfilterindex.lisp:132) it never reports the gap and the connect hook's stall warning never fires.
consequence: The finding's stated impact -- 'gettxspendingprevout reports an output as spent by a transaction that is not in the active chain' -- is REFUTED: %txospender-confirmed-spender already discards any locator whose block is not on the active chain (src/rpc/mempool.lisp:439-455, the %block-on-active-chain-p guard), so the abandoned branch's leftover rows are inert, and my probe confirms they answer nothing. What the missing rewind actually costs is the opposite and worse: the blocks of the NEW active chain between the fork point and the marker's height are never indexed, permanently, and gettxspendingprevout then answers that an output IS UNSPENT when a confirmed transaction on the active chain spends it. That is the silent direction -- Core's rpc/mempool.cpp shape returns the bare {txid, vout} for 'nothing spent it' (src/rpc/mempool.lisp:415-424), which is indistinguishable from a genuine answer. It is permanent because the connect hook keeps moving the marker forward over the gap with no contiguity refusal, so every later restart sees index-height >= tip and skips the backfill again. Preconditions bound it: -txospenderindex is opt-in (default off) and the branch switch must happen while the process is DOWN (a crash or kill with the index ahead of the flushed chainstate, or an invalidateblock/reorg across a restart) -- an online reorg is handled by the :block-disconnected hook. Given the rubric (a wrong index answer reaching an operator), the false 'unspent' is S2, not the S3 the finding filed.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3b, warm image, probe build/ga11probe/tsi.lisp. Built a regtest node fixture with two branches from genesis at heights 1-2: branch A (abandoned) whose two blocks each spend outpoint A0:0, branch B (active) whose two blocks each spend outpoint B0:0, all four blocks stored and index-entered, then update-chain-tip to B's tip at height 2 while the index marker names A's tip at height 2. Result: (:TIP 2 :PREPARE-SYNC-RETURNED NIL :INDEX-HEIGHT-BEFORE 2 :CATCH-UP-RETURNED NIL :INDEX-HEIGHT-AFTER 2 :STALE-BRANCH-A-ENTRIES 2 :ACTIVE-BRANCH-B-ENTRIES 0 :RPC-FINDS-CONFIRMED-SPENDER NIL :CONTROL-CATCH-UP-RETURNED 3 :CONTROL-BRANCH-B-ENTRIES 2 :CONTROL-RPC-FINDS-SPENDER T). So: prepare-sync is the base no-op; catch-up-index does nothing; branch B's spends are never recorded; %txospender-confirmed-spender answers NIL for an outpoint the ACTIVE tip spends. The positive control (index-clear-best, i.e. what a rewind would achieve) makes the same catch-up index 3 blocks and the RPC then finds the spender, so the probe discriminates. The stale branch-A rows survive (2 locators) but the RPC filters them, which is what refutes the filed impact. Ours: src/storage/txospenderindex.lisp:52-72, :233-255; src/node/indexes.lisp:22-50, :61-88, :90-114, :226-251; src/storage/index-base.lisp:115-121; src/rpc/mempool.lisp:415-455. Core at d3056bc: index/base.cpp:201-247 (Sync), :239 (the Rewind trigger), :290-320 (Rewind/CustomRemove); index/txospenderindex.cpp:73-78 (disconnect_data), :136-139 (CustomRemove).
fix_shape: Give txospender-index an INDEX-PREPARE-SYNC method that is Core's BaseIndex::Sync rewind, and make its INDEX-HEIGHT chainstate-aware so the backfill guard cannot be satisfied by an off-chain marker. Concretely: read the stored (hash, height); look the hash up in the header index; if it is absent or not an ancestor of the active tip, walk back to the fork point (the coinstatsindex already has %coinstatsindex-fork-height for exactly this, src/node/indexes.lisp:129+, so reuse it rather than writing a second walk), read each block of the abandoned branch from the block store and call txospenderindex-remove-block on it -- Core's Rewind -> CustomRemove, which is exact for this index because both sides build the outpoint list from the block alone -- then set the best marker to the fork point so the existing INDEX-SYNC backfills forward. Where the branch's blocks are no longer readable (pruned), clear the marker and rebuild rather than leaving a gap. Second, make INDEX-HEIGHT return -1 (or the fork height) when the stored hash is not on the active chain, so catch-up-index's (< height tip) guard can never be satisfied by an off-chain marker even if prepare-sync is skipped. Third, give INDEX-WRITE-BLOCK the :noncontiguous refusal blockfilterindex already returns, so a gap is at least logged once instead of being papered over by the next connect. The regression test must assert the false-negative direction -- an outpoint spent on the active chain is FOUND after a restart whose marker sat on an abandoned branch -- since the existing reorg test only covers the online disconnect path.
